units.translation: a tunic in imitation of a Liburnian cloak.
I remember. Aeschylus used only the forms of this verb that recall the present μνάομαι [to be mindful], the perfect μέμνημαι [I remember], and the aorist ἐμνησάμην [I remembered, I made mention].
ὑπομιμνήσκεις [you remind] is corrupt at line 989, where the meter requires ὑποφαίνεις [you reveal] or another word of the same length.
Alas, how I groan when I remember Athens.
I remember hearing about your pride.
I will be careful to remember these cherished commands of yours.

Remembering the former toils, a Doric form, of which the other example is Ch. 623, where in M we have ἐπεμνήσαμεν [we remembered] (wrongly for ἐπεμνησάμην [I remembered], which Heath restored), but with an η written above, so that it should be written ἐπεμνασάμαν [I remembered], unless Aeschylus was content to use the Doric ending | ἐπεμνησάμαν [I remembered].
I have now been reminded of such things as these.
The tragedians used μίμνω [to remain] for μένω [to remain] when the meter required it, from which rule Aeschylus departed in only three places.
remaining at the exits of the gates.
they remain where the Asopus waters the plain with its streams, and

it remains for the doer to suffer at the throne of Zeus while he remains, unless we should write μένοντες [remaining] and μένουσι [they remain], and in the third place, where in the strophe (1533) an iambus corresponds, μένει [he remains], as Heimsoeth did.
For fearful wrath remains, returning again.
For me remains a cleft with a double-edged spear.
And for him who remains, suffering blooms.
Remain in the face of these things.
There neither wind allows to remain nor to sail out.
and bull-voiced, fearful imitators bellow from somewhere unseen.
faulty for viv. See under the word í p. 161.
shedding tears from my heart, which wastes away as I weep.
opinions melting away upon the earth waste away without honor.

Hesychius: μινύρονται [they warble]: προφωνοῦσι [they proclaim], προλέγουσι [they foretell], which L. Dindorf in the Thesaurus conjectured should be restored for κινύρονται [they lament] at Sept. 123.
whenever I think I should sing or warble.
they warble: they proclaim, they foretell
uttering shrill sounds in grievous misfortune.
having been persuaded by the gifts of Minos.
it is fitting to accompany the dithyramb with mixed shouting.
A word not read elsewhere, which the scholiast explains as ἐκ πάσης συμμιγούς ἡλικίας [from every mixed age].
of the people being destroyed with mixed shouting.
seeing a creature, a hateful monster mixed with human form.
for I have learned to hate traitors.
